messages:
elaine_support: FYI — TupleHealth just escalated: they see 5-10s tail latency and intermittent 401s when hitting our /v1/generate endpoint. Started ~08:12 UTC. They say requests often go to us-west though their org is EU-only.

mike_oncall: Copy. Any customer repro steps or headers they shared?

elaine_support: Yes. They provided a curl that reproduces from their EU cloud function. They see x-redwood-region: eu-west in the request but responses show x-served-region: us-west and x-envoy-upstream-service-time high. Quote: "curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Request-ID: th-85' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate". Logged response headers: 

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-served-region: us-west-2
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 4823
content-length: 1234
```

elaine_support: They also saw a flurry of 401s earlier with header: x-auth-rewritten: true — they think traffic is hitting a fallback path that strips/rewrites auth.

ryan_infra: Noted. Sending to infra + network. Nina, do we have any recent Envoy LB config changes or rollout that could cause region mismatch / header rewrite?

nina_network: We pushed an Envoy config change yesterday to support new header-based routing fallback (when primary region overloaded). But that should match x-redwood-region before fallback. I'll pull the rollout logs.

ops-bot: [ALERT] 08:11 UTC — spike in 5xx/latency for /v1/generate in eu-west target group. Canary rollback staged: false.

mike_oncall: Can we reproduce internally? I'll curl from eu-west host in our infra.

mike_oncall: (after repro) Repro'd — from eu-west host with x-redwood-region: eu-west-1 the request still routed to us-west-2. Looks like the Envoy route matcher is ignoring the header sometimes.

sarah_eng_platform: This smells like L7 header matcher instability under load. We recently added an "exists" matcher to fallback rule. If header exists -> route to eu backend, else fallback to global. If upstream is transiently slow, maybe we hit fallback but header still present and gets rewritten. Any traffic logs showing whether the header arrived at the edge?

ryan_infra: I pulled raw edge logs. TupleHealth's request reached edge with x-redwood-region: eu-west-1. But at our gateway (envoy) outgoing requests to upstream show different headers: x-auth-rewritten: true and missing x-redwood-region. So a filter is dropping or rewriting headers during fallback path.

nina_network: Confirmed. I see a mixture in the envoy proxy logs: some connections go through the new header-based router, others go through a legacy L7 listener. The legacy listener has a header-cleaning filter we forgot to port. Under connection churn the load balancer is flapping between listeners.

elaine_support: Customer is asking for a mitigation. They want us to route their live traffic only to eu endpoints until fix.

sarah_eng_platform: Two options: 1) Policy override for that org id to force region routing at our control plane (fast) or 2) rollback the new listener config (safer) to stop header-cleaning behavior. I recommend quick control-plane override for TupleHealth plus an emergency rollback if we see more customers.

omar_billing: Heads up — if we force egress to eu, cost will spike but should be temporary. Keep me in loop for any billing re-assignments.

mike_oncall: Applying policy pin for org tuplehealth (org-id: org_th_123) to prefer eu-west backends. Pushing now.

ops-bot: [ACTION] 08:28 UTC — policy change applied for org_th_123: route_preference=eu-west-1.

mike_oncall: Can TupleHealth confirm now?

elaine_support: Reply from customer: "latency back to normal and 401s stopped. Thanks — please keep us pinned until patch." :thumbsup:

ryan_infra: Good. I'll open an infra ticket to rollback the partial listener rollout. Nina, can you coordinate? We should also add a test in the LB integration tests for header persistence during failover.

nina_network: Will do. Plan: immediate rollback of the listener plugin in canary, then full rollback if no blockers. Also add end-to-end test to ensure x-redwood-region persists to upstream and that no filter strips auth headers on fallback.

sarah_eng_platform: I'll add a canary job to simulate header-based routing churn and assert header invariants. Also ticketing note: verify that our fallback path doesn't rewrite Authorization or inject x-auth-rewritten header.

omar_billing: Also add a note to customer billing if we exceed committed spend because of forced routing.

mike_oncall: Postmortem/incident doc needed if rollback goes prod-wide. I'll start a stub in /incidents.

elaine_support: Thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated and close the escalation once rollback + tests are in.

nina_network: Follow-up: found race in Envoy listener selection; created PR to remove legacy header-cleaning filter and added metrics to detect listener-flap. ETA patch + rollout 3h.

ryan_infra: Nice. Add the PR link and the test plan to the incident doc.

elaine_support: Closing loop — TupleHealth confirmed stable at 09:10 UTC. I'll mark the thread resolved in support queue but keep the ticket open until postmortem. :white_check_mark:
